page: Microsoft Azure F8-2amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famdsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 2 physical cores and 2 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 945 GB local disk, and the server is premium storage capable. No GPUs are present in this configuration.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, geekbench single-core score, and single-threaded gzip compression all ranking in the top tier. However, multi-threaded and multi-core scaling is limited due to the 2-vCPU hardware constraint. Multi-core stress-ng performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and memory bandwidth metrics fall into the average tier. Tradeoffs are evident in highly parallelized tasks, where bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, software compilation with clang, and static web serving throughput register in the weak tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F8-2amds_v7 offers high resource density for memory-bound applications that do not require massive parallel processing. The combination of a fast 4.5 GHz single-core speed and 64.0 GB of RAM makes it suitable for memory-intensive workloads with low thread concurrency. Recommended workloads include database operations, caching layers such as Redis, text processing, and lightweight memory-heavy data processing. It is less suitable for highly parallelized compute tasks, ray tracing, or large-scale web serving.
